title: The Umbrella Shelf
passage:
On rainy days, the entrance of Hikari Community Center became crowded with wet umbrellas. There was one large umbrella stand, but many umbrellas looked similar. People often spent several minutes searching when they left, and once in a while someone accidentally took the wrong one. The staff considered putting numbered tags on every umbrella, but that would require someone to manage the tags all day.

A volunteer named Mari suggested a simpler idea. Instead of one large stand, they could divide umbrellas into several groups. The center already had an unused wooden shelf with six sections. They placed a waterproof tray under it and labeled the sections with easy pictures: sun, moon, tree, bird, fish, and star. Visitors could choose any section and remember the picture.

The first rainy day showed one problem. Most children wanted to use the star and bird sections, so those became crowded while other spaces stayed empty. The staff changed the sign. It now asked visitors to use the least crowded section. They also placed a small card at the reception desk with the six pictures so people could point to the one they had chosen if they forgot its name.

The new system did not completely prevent mistakes. Two identical black umbrellas were still confused one afternoon. After that, Mari added a basket of reusable colored bands that visitors could loosely wrap around a handle. The bands were not required, but they helped people with common umbrella designs.

By the end of the rainy season, the entrance was easier to use. The solution had cost almost nothing because the center reused a shelf and simple materials it already owned. Mari liked the project because it showed that organization can solve a problem even when technology is unnecessary. The center did not need a digital ticket machine or a complicated rule. It needed a way to break one crowded space into smaller, memorable choices. Sometimes a simple picture is enough to make a shared place work better.
translation:
雨の日、ひかり公民館の入口は濡れた傘で混雑していました。大きな傘立てが一つありましたが、似た傘が多く、帰る時に探すのに時間がかかり、ときには間違えて持ち帰る人もいました。番号札を付ける案も出ましたが、一日中管理する人が必要になります。

ボランティアのマリは、傘をいくつかのグループに分けるという単純な方法を提案しました。使っていない六区画の木製棚に防水トレーを置き、太陽、月、木、鳥、魚、星の絵を付けました。来館者は好きな区画へ入れ、その絵を覚えます。

最初の雨の日、子どもたちが星と鳥へ集中し、そこだけ混雑しました。そこで『一番空いている区画を使ってください』と表示を変え、受付には六つの絵のカードを置き、名前を忘れても指させるようにしました。

完全に間違いがなくなったわけではありません。同じ黒い傘が取り違えられたこともあり、持ち手へ軽く巻ける再利用可能な色バンドを追加しました。必須ではありませんが、よく似た傘の区別に役立ちました。

梅雨の終わりには入口が使いやすくなっていました。古い棚と手元の材料を再利用したため費用はほとんどかかりませんでした。マリは、この計画から、技術を使わなくても『整理の仕方』で問題を解けることがあると学びました。複雑な機械ではなく、一つの混雑した場所を覚えやすい小さな選択肢へ分けるだけでよかったのです。
